Definition: a primary verb; to close (literally or figuratively):--shut (up).
KeyPassages: Matthew 6:6; Luke 4:25; John 20:19; Acts 5:23; 1 John 3:17; Revelation 3:7
BiblicalUsage: Kleio means to shut, to close. Matthew 6:6 says when thou prayest, shut thy door and pray to thy Father in secret, Luke 4:25 recalls the heaven shut up three years and six months in the days of Elias, and John 20:19 has Jesus standing in the midst though the doors were shut for fear of the Jews. Acts 5:23 finds the prison shut with all safety and the keepers standing without, yet no man within, 1 John 3:17 warns the man who shutteth up his bowels of compassion from his brother, and Revelation 3:7 praises Him that openeth, and no man shutteth, and shutteth, and no man openeth.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe shutting is the test of the heart: the door shut for prayer is holy, the heart shut against a brother is not. I hold that the doors shut against Jesus in John 20:19 could not keep Him out, and the prison shut in Acts 5:23 could not keep His apostles in.
RelatedBooks: Matthew; Luke; John; Acts; 1 John; Revelation
